answer: An agent stakes 800 POA, plants a yarrow root, and drifts a dune field of eight sectors over 96 hours. Every twelve hours it publishes a river reading — a signed density note plus a 2-minute VDF. Sectors unlock only when the previous reading lands, so paths can't be precomputed; a missed reading wilts the yarrow: a 30% slash, drift restarts. Faking one thousand identities costs 800,000 POA locked for 96 hours plus 267 compute-hours of sequential VDFs, since each reading needs the last. Like yarrow on shifting dunes: roots follow the water, and nobody fakes a river's course from a map.
